eyebrow: ServiceNow Security & Access Controls · Chapter Six
subtitle: Lesson 20 · Governance, Compliance & Audit

eyebrow: Four frameworks worth knowing by name
code:
SOC 2     -- trust criteria commonly expected of any SaaS vendor
HIPAA     -- relevant once PHI touches the instance
GDPR      -- relevant for any EU individual's personal data
PCI-DSS   -- relevant if payment card data ever touches the instance
caption: Which frameworks apply depends on what the instance actually holds.

code:
What the platform provides:          What the customer owns:
- Encryption (edge, column-level)    - Deciding WHICH fields need it
- Audit logging (sys_audit)          - Deciding WHICH fields to audit
- ACLs, field-level security         - Designing the role/ACL model
- Masking, export controls           - Applying rules to the right data

Capability exists <> Compliance achieved.
caption: The gap between the two is entirely configuration and operation.

code:
SOC 2:     expected by customers/auditors of any SaaS vendor
HIPAA:     triggered by protected health information (PHI)
GDPR:      triggered by EU individuals' personal data
PCI-DSS:   triggered by payment card data touching the instance
caption: Which frameworks apply depends on the specific data in play.

eyebrow: "We use ServiceNow" is not a compliance claim
code:
Analogy:
  Owning a bank vault  -/->  sound financial controls
  Running ServiceNow   -/->  automatic compliance

What actually matters: who configured it, how access is
reviewed, and whether evidence exists on request.
caption: A real team has to configure, operate, and evidence the controls.
